w10_P4_001694: A rail workshop's test summary is the energy carried by a runaway trolley, expressed in kilojoules, plus 7 kJ charged to the brake heater. The trolley has a mass of 41 kg. It runs at a speed, in metres per second, equal to twice a certain count. That count is the number of different pairs of tie-down points that can be chosen from the 9 tie-down points welded to the trolley floor, taking 2 at a time. What is the test summary figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001696: A cannery's balance sheet ends with the energy of a full carousel expressed in kilojoules, less 4 kJ drawn by the labeller. A full carousel holds 12 identical pucks, so it carries 12 times the energy of a single puck. Each puck has a mass of 36 kg and slides along the deck at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 336 and 19 exactly. The cannery works this balance out at the end of every shift. What figure does the balance sheet end with, in kJ?
w10_P4_001698: A cable test bench tracks a shuttle whose position along the guide, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 3 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The bench reads how fast the shuttle is moving at the instant 3 seconds in, subtracts 26 from that reading, and multiplies the remainder by 4 to obtain the launch speed, in metres per second, used for the next stage. The launched body has a mass of 12 kg. The bench's control lamp draws 45 W. The stage total is the body's kinetic energy plus 14 J allowed for the trigger, and the bench performs 6 identical stages in a run. How much energy does a full run account for, in J?
w10_P4_001704: A wind-tunnel logbook's closing entry takes the model's kinetic energy, subtracts 21 J for the sting heater, adds 19 J for the balance supply, and then adds a further 1 J for the datalogger. The model has a mass of 31000 g. Its speed in metres per second is taken from a calibration chart on which a plotted quantity equals 3 times the cube of the dial setting minus 1 times the square of the dial setting; the speed is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 2. The tunnel's contraction section is 4 m long. What is the logbook's closing entry, in J?
w10_P4_001718: A go-kart club's season figure is 5 times the energy of a single race start, expressed in kilojoules. At a start, a kart and driver of combined mass 29 kg leave the line at a speed, in metres per second, found by taking a number x, adding 9, and then adding 16. The number x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 3 times x, plus 2, comes to exactly 0. The club's main straight is 180 m long. What is the club's season figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001721: On a factory test bench a carriage of mass 43 kg is released along a level rail. Its speed in metres per second is 3 times a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 5 times x, plus 4, equals exactly 0. The bench releases 12 identical carriages in each test, so a test involves 12 times the energy of one carriage. The bench's report then adds 27 kJ for the compressor that recharges the launcher between tests. What total does the bench's report give for one test, in kJ?
w10_P4_001724: A model-rocket club fires a dart of mass 3000 g from a rail launcher on the test field. The dart's speed in metres per second is taken from the launcher's calibration curve, on which a plotted quantity equals 5 times the cube of the pressure-dial reading plus 6 times the square of that reading; the speed is the second-order rate of change of the plotted quantity with respect to the dial reading, evaluated at a dial reading of 1. The club fires 6 identical darts in a volley, so a volley carries 6 times the energy of a single dart. From the volley total the club subtracts 16 J absorbed by the launch rail. Expressed in kilojoules, the field log then adds 8 kJ for the compressor that repressurises the launcher. What does the field log record, in kJ?
w10_P4_001731: A ski-jump training rig sends a sled of mass 24 kg down the ramp. The sled's speed in metres per second is 3 more than a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 7 times x, plus 6, equals exactly 0. The rig completes 11 identical descents in a session, so a session carries 11 times the energy of a single descent. The session log then subtracts 21 J for the winch brake and a further 20 J for the timing gates. The ramp itself is 55 m long. What does the session log record, in J?
w10_P4_001738: A cold-store audit ends with the energy of one carousel cycle expressed in kilojoules, less 28 kJ booked to the defrost heater. A cycle runs 10 identical trays, so it carries 10 times the energy of a single tray. Each tray has a mass of 35 kg and slides at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 255 and 55 exactly. The store's aisle lighting is rated at 90 W. What figure does the audit end with, in kJ?
w10_P4_001740: A hobby workshop's tally is 6 times a certain net energy figure, because the same test is repeated on 6 benches. The net figure for one bench is the puck's kinetic energy less 29 J drawn by the release solenoid. Each puck has a mass of 2 kg. A puck is fired at a speed, in metres per second, equal to 5 times the largest whole number that divides both 359 and 154 exactly. What is the workshop's tally, in J?
w10_P4_001743: A dockside crane logs a trial in which a test block of mass 55000 g is released along a level runway. The block's speed in metres per second equals the total accumulated by the flow meter between the 0th and the 1st second of the trial, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 5 times t. The trial sheet takes the block's kinetic energy, adds 9 J for the release gear, and then subtracts 4 J for the brake bleed. Converted to kilojoules, the dockside's daily entry then adds 3 kJ for the crane's standby load. What is the daily entry, in kJ?
w10_P4_001745: A conveyor rig accelerates a pallet of mass 125 kg along a level track. The pallet's acceleration in metres per second squared equals the total that the drive's meter accumulates between the 1st and the 2nd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 3 times t. The rig's log takes the driving force, adds 9 N for the chain pretension, and then adds a further 30 N for the guide-roller drag. The rig's control cabinet is rated at 400 W. What figure does the rig's log give, in kN?
w10_P4_001746: At a hydro test station a float of mass 31000 g is carried along a channel. The float's speed in metres per second equals the volume the channel gauge accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second of a surge, where the gauge's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 6 times t. The station's energy sheet takes the float's kinetic energy in kilojoules and adds 23 kJ drawn by the pump. It then adds a further 28 kJ drawn by the chiller. What total does the energy sheet show, in kJ?
w10_P4_001767: A bottling plant receives 278 caps of one type and 92 of another, and it packs them into identical boxes using the largest box size that divides both counts exactly. A test slug of mass 52000 g then moves along the runout at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that box size. The plant runs 8 identical runouts at the same time, so the floor carries 8 times the energy of one slug, expressed in kilojoules. The plant's summary then adds 24 kJ for the air compressor. What does the plant's summary give, in kJ?
w10_P4_001776: A tyre factory receives 242 valves of one kind and 165 of another, and it packs them in identical cartons using the largest carton size that divides both counts exactly. A test mass of 129000 g on the factory's shaker is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that carton size. The engineering sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons and subtracts 24 kN allowed for the shaker's own reaction frame. The factory runs 10 identical shakers, and the sheet reports 10 times the single-shaker figure. What does the engineering sheet report, in kN?
w10_P4_001777: A theme-park operator's report is the park's energy figure plus 17 kJ charged to the ticket hall. The park's figure is 4 times a train's figure, since 4 identical trains run at once, and a train's figure is 8 times a single car's energy, since each train is made up of 8 cars. A loaded car has a mass of 27000 g. Its speed at the bottom of the drop, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 30, equals exactly 0. What does the operator's report give, in kJ?
w10_P4_001781: A quarry crusher drives a jaw of mass 117 kg. The jaw's acceleration in metres per second squared equals the total the drive meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second of a stroke, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 6 times t. The maintenance sheet subtracts 19 N for the return-spring preload, and the crusher has 8 such jaws sharing one frame, so the frame takes 8 times the corrected figure. The crusher's feed chute is 4 m long. Expressed in kilonewtons, the sheet finally subtracts 6 kN for the mounting bolts. What does the maintenance sheet end with, in kN?
w10_P4_001783: A shipyard rig accelerates a test carriage of mass 177000 g along a level track. The carriage's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 10 times the value, plus 24, is exactly 0. Five identical carriages are coupled into a set, three sets run on each track, and the yard operates 6 identical tracks at the same time. What total force do all the yard's drives supply, in kN?
w10_P4_001786: A physics club's demonstration cart has a mass of 6000 g and runs along a level bench. Its speed in metres per second is found by taking a number x, subtracting 12, and then adding 6, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 14, equals exactly 0. The club's energy sheet expresses the cart's kinetic energy in kilojoules. It then adds 15 kJ drawn by the bench's air supply over the course of the demonstration. What does the club's energy sheet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001801: A rail freight yard's annual figure is 4 times its monthly figure, and the monthly figure is 11 times the energy of a single train. A train is made up of 8 identical wagons, so it carries 8 times the energy of one wagon. Each wagon has a mass of 15 kg on the scale model used for the estimate. A wagon's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 4th second of a run, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 3 times t. What is the yard's annual figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001804: A haulage test rig records a sled's speed in metres per second as 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 5 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The rig reads how fast that speed is changing at the instant 2 seconds in, then subtracts 26 to obtain the acceleration, in metres per second squared, that it applies to the load. The load has a mass of 159000 g, and the rig's cooling fan draws 120 W. Eleven identical rigs drive the same load in parallel, so the hall takes 11 times the single-rig force, and the log then subtracts 25 N for the frame's own reaction. What does the log record, in kN?
w10_P4_001805: A machine shop's balance line reads the drive force in kilonewtons, adds 15 kN for the clamping ram, and then subtracts 16 kN for the counterweight. The driven slide has a mass of 41 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 65 and 315 exactly. The shop takes this balance reading before every production run. What does the balance line read, in kN?
w10_P4_001808: A bobsleigh centre launches a test sled of mass 51000 g. The sled's launch speed in metres per second is twice the sum of the two track-gate readings, which are 2 and 13. The centre launches 11 sleds in a session, runs 7 sessions in a day, and operates 5 identical tracks at once. The centre's timing beam draws 60 W. How much energy do all the launches across the centre account for in a day, in kJ?
w10_P4_001818: A launch bench tracks a puck whose distance along the rail, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 1 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the bench uses how fast the puck is moving at the instant 1 second after release. The puck has a mass of 26000 g. The bench's indicator lamp draws 90 W. The bench's energy sheet takes the puck's kinetic energy, subtracts 5 J for the release catch, adds 2 J credited to the sensor, and then subtracts 27 J for the return spring. What does the energy sheet total, in J?
w10_P4_001822: A depot's shift report gives the total force taken by 10 identical frames, each frame carrying 7 identical actuators pulling together. One actuator drives a slide of mass 71000 g. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 190 and 177 exactly. The depot's inspection lamp is rated at 55 W. What total force does the shift report give, in kN?
